clue.text: Google is used by setter as I haven't a clue!

parts.note: to google something is to look it up online, to hunt for it
the setter writing the clue refers to themselves, so the pronoun for the writer

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler admits to leaning on a search engine because they are stumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is used by' simply places one piece beside the other. The definition is the exclamation at the end, a nice joke in a crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are colloquial exclamations of ignorance, said with a shrug when asked something you cannot answer.

clue.text: Those starting in school are nursed here

definitions.text: Those starting in school are nursed here

indicators.note: asks for the letters that begin each of the following words

explanation.surface: The youngest pupils at a school are looked after in a particular place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those starting in' takes the opening letters of the next three words, and the whole clue describes the result: the sickroom of a British boarding school, short for sanatorium.
explanation.definitionFit: It is British school slang for the sickroom or sanatorium where unwell pupils are cared for.

clue.text: Mature pudding from a long time in the past

definitions.text: a long time in the past

parts.note: to mature is to age, as wine or cheese does
sago is a starchy milk pudding, a British school-dinner staple

explanation.surface: A well-kept dessert surviving from some distant era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mature' looks like an adjective describing the pudding but is a verb here. Sago is a milk pudding made from palm starch, familiar from old British school dinners.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverbial phrase meaning far back in history, a synonym for long since.

clue.text: Character keeps time in class

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an eccentric person is called a character or a case
T is the standard abbreviation for time in physics

explanation.surface: An eccentric pupil is punctual during lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary social rank, especially in Hindu society, is a division or stratum of people.

clue.text: Sounds like bloke rejected for bulk distribution

indicators.note: tells us the phrase is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: bloke is British slang for a man, a male
something rejected is out, as an idea ruled out of consideration

explanation.surface: It seems a man has been turned down for a wholesale delivery job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' applies to the word for a bloke, British slang for a man; the word for rejected then follows as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass sending of letters or leaflets to many addresses at once, a mailshot.

clue.text: Agent dealing with Charlie has backed derrick mostly

indicators.note: backed tells us the letters are turned to run the other way
mostly means we take most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: a derrick is a kind of crane for lifting loads

explanation.surface: A spy handling a contact called Charlie has largely supported a man named Derrick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims CRANE to CRAN, and 'backed' turns that round. Charlie is slang for cocaine, so the agent is a drugs officer.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a narcotics officer, whose business is cocaine and other drugs.

clue.text: Benign tumour on a dame needing treatment

indicators.note: something needing treatment must be worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A harmless growth on a titled lady requires medical attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term for a non-cancerous growth of glandular tissue.

clue.text: Hit rock's first for sergeant and privates

parts.note: to crown someone is to hit them on the head
a rock is slang for a gem, especially a diamond

indicators.note: first for asks for the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A pop group's debut single is a smash with every rank in the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first for' takes the opening letter of sergeant. The privates are not soldiers but slang for a man's genitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are humorous slang euphemisms for the male genitals.

clue.text: Nitrogen in unopened pickle is concerning

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other
unopened means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a pickle is a difficult situation, a mire
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Gas found inside a sealed jar of preserves is a worrying sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' takes the M off MIRE to leave IRE, and 'in' puts N inside it. 'Concerning' looks like worrying but means about.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal Latin phrase meaning in the matter of, or about.

clue.text: Boy keeping wicket tickled with it

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the other pieces go within this one

parts.note: a boy is someone's son
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket
something that tickled caused a light irritation, it itched

explanation.surface: A lad playing wicketkeeper at cricket is amused by something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs 'keeping wicket' together as the cricket position behind the stumps, and 'tickled with it' as amused; 'keeping' is really the container signal and 'with it' means trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal phrases for being alert and aware of the latest trends.

clue.text: Shift work scheme engages one

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or take in, so one piece is taken inside
to work something is to knead or manipulate it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A rota-based employment programme takes on a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges SCHEME into CHEMSE and 'engages' takes I inside it. The shift is a garment, not a working period.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose straight dress or undergarment is an example of this loose-fitting slip.

clue.text: All there outside look for a fashionable young woman

indicators.note: outside tells us this piece goes around the other

parts.note: someone all there is of sound mind, sane
lo is an old exclamation meaning look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Everyone is waiting out in the street for a glimpse of a stylish girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is 1980s British slang for a wealthy, fashionable young Londoner, named after a square in Chelsea; 'outside' is the container signal, not a place to wait.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an upper-class, stylish girl from the Chelsea set, short for a Ranger of that name.

clue.text: First dance with nothing on may go down like this!

definitions.note: the phrase points at a proverbial comparison for something that fails with its audience

parts.note: to be first is to be in the lead
a ball is a formal dance
nothing is zero, written as the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Opening the ball naked risks a very poor reception.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom: a joke or idea that fails utterly is said to go down like this heavy, unflyable object.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something received very badly compares it to this impossibly heavy airship.

clue.text: No other person present in the form of 11

wordplay.reading: a figure 1 placed next to a figure 1

parts.note: the number is read as its two digits, each the same figure, set side by side

explanation.surface: Nobody else has turned up, judging by the look of the answer to clue eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the form of' asks us to look at the shape of the number rather than at clue 11: it is the same digit written beside itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a private meeting between just two people, with nobody else in the room.

clue.text: Awfully long wait for French coach?

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are in a bad state and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A terribly lengthy delay for a bus or a sports trainer from France.
explanation.walkthrough: The coach is a railway carriage, and the answer is the French term for a sleeping car, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The French name for a railway sleeping carriage on Continental trains.

clue.text: Finals put aside, girl is permitted to meet boy in Italian theatre

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its last letter before they are joined

parts.note: a lass is a girl, especially in Scotland and northern England
someone who is permitted to do something can do it
a lad is a boy or young man

explanation.surface: With exams over, a young woman is allowed a date with a lad at a playhouse in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finals put aside' removes the last letter of each of LASS, CAN and LAD, leaving LAS, CA and LA. Finals in the surface are university exams.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous opera house in Milan is an example of a playhouse in Italy.

clue.text: A geriatric's true statement represented

parts.note: an old person could truthfully say 'I'm' followed by a word for old
the second word of that sentence, a synonym for elderly

explanation.surface: An honest declaration by an old person was delivered on their behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: Imagine what a very old person could honestly say about themselves in two words, then run the words together.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict or picture something is to portray it, here in the past tense.

clue.text: Copper in a station endlessly? You could count on this once

definitions.text: You could count on this once

indicators.note: in tells us this piece sits inside the others
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a station is a base, as in a military or research post
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman stuck at the nick for ever was formerly a dependable sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Counting on something reads as relying, but is meant literally: sums were once done on it. 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the station word and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on wires, formerly the standard tool for doing arithmetic.

clue.text: Refurbished entrance not right for eatery

indicators.note: something refurbished has been done up anew, so the letters are rearranged
not tells us the following letter is absent from the fodder

explanation.surface: The redecorated doorway is unsuitable for a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' takes the R out of ENTRANCE, and 'Refurbished' rearranges the remaining ENTANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff or school dining room is an example of a place to eat.

clue.text: Scores disappeared during matches

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so one piece falls within the other

parts.note: cup ties are matches in a knockout competition
something that disappeared went, as in 'the pain went'

explanation.surface: The goal tallies vanished while the games were being played.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is an old word for twenty, so the definition is a plural number, not goal tallies; 'during' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is an old word for a group of 20, so the plurals correspond.

clue.text: Seasonal visitors, informally those against leaving nag's head

parts.note: in casual or dialect speech 'them' replaces 'those', as in 'them apples'

indicators.note: leaving tells us the following letter departs from the word before

parts.note: agin is a dialect form of against, also covered by the clue's 'informally'

indicators.note: head asks for the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Christmas guests, loosely the ones opposed to abandoning the top end of a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'informally' covers both colloquial forms, THEM and AGIN. 'head' takes N from nag's, and 'leaving' removes it from AGIN to give AGI.
explanation.definitionFit: The three wise men who came to Bethlehem appear every Christmas in nativity scenes.

clue.text: There's a lot more fluctuating in this stop

indicators.note: fluctuating means shifting about, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: Passenger numbers vary far more at this particular station.
explanation.walkthrough: The stop is an organ stop, a control that here produces a wavering effect, so 'fluctuating' also colours the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ control giving a trembling, wavering sound.

clue.text: Note a leg injured — a stretcher will do

definitions.note: read as 'what a device that stretches will do', pointing at a verb

indicators.note: something injured is damaged, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Observe a hurt limb, and decide that carrying the patient off is good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The stretcher is not for casualties: it is anything that stretches, and the definition is the action it performs.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen or draw something out is the action of anything that pulls a thing longer.

clue.text: Milk producer, one in French city

indicators.note: in tells us this piece sits inside the place named

parts.note: Brest is a port city in Brittany
one can be the indefinite article a

explanation.surface: A dairy farmer, a single person living in a town in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The mammary gland is the organ that makes a mother's supply for her baby.

clue.text: Malicious woman in scrap with child

parts.note: a scrap is a small piece, a bit
ch is the abbreviation for child used in family trees

explanation.surface: A spiteful mother caught up in a fight, her kid alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive slang term for a spiteful or unpleasant female.

clue.text: Differing greatly from some Europeans?

parts.note: an idiom for being utterly unlike is read as being separated from the people of Warsaw and Krakow

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means holding utterly opposed views, as far from each other as the ends of the earth; it also reads as away from natives of Poland.

clue.text: Indirectly, they make waves in uproar sometimes

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Troublemakers who stir things up in a roundabout way during the occasional commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the answer as lying within 'uproar sometimes'. Rowing blades disturb the water, so they make ripples as a side effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing blades disturb the water as a by-product of propelling a boat.

clue.text: Person who's taken in by centre-forward?

definitions.text: Person who's taken in by centre-forward?

indicators.note: something taken in by a word is contained within its letters

explanation.surface: Someone fooled by a striker's dive on the football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' marks the answer as lying inside centre-forward, and the whole clue also describes it: the match official a striker tries to fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The match official in football is the one a diving striker hopes to deceive.

clue.text: How choice list gets to me, unlike an aristocrat

definitions.note: describes speech or manners that the upper class would not use

parts.words: How choice list gets to me
parts.note: a list of choices is a menu, which becomes 'me' when it has none of its last two letters: the first word of that description, a negative

parts.words: How choice list gets to me
parts.note: the pair of letters that the word for a list of dishes must lose to leave 'me'

explanation.surface: The effect a set of options has on me, not being of noble birth.
explanation.walkthrough: MENU becomes ME by losing its last two letters; say what was done in two short words and you have the answer. U and its opposite are 1950s British labels for upper-class and not upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A British label for vocabulary and habits that are not upper-class.

clue.text: Evening without work, close to a couple of females

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near or close
F is the abbreviation for female, so two of them is FF

explanation.surface: A free evening spent near a pair of women.
explanation.definitionFit: A break from a late shift, a free few hours after dark.
